q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Finance Bill from the Appropriation Bill presented after the Budget?

options.A: The Finance Bill authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India, while the Appropriation Bill gives effect to the taxation proposals
options.B: Both Bills can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha
options.C: The Appropriation Bill is passed before the Demands for Grants are voted by the Lok Sabha
options.D: The Finance Bill gives effect to the financial (taxation) proposals of the Government, while the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet the grants and charged expenditure

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India completes his report on the accounts of a State for a financial year. Under Article 151 of the Constitution, that report is submitted to:

options.A: The Governor of the State, who causes them to be laid before the State Legislature
options.C: The Chief Minister of the State
options.D: The Public Accounts Committee of Parliament

q: The President is required by Article 280 of the Constitution to constitute a Finance Commission at regular intervals. That constitution must take place:

options.A: Every year, along with the Annual Financial Statement
options.B: At the expiration of every fifth year, or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary
options.D: Only on the recommendation of the Inter-State Council

q: A Money Bill is sought to be introduced in the Rajya Sabha without the recommendation of the President. The correct constitutional position is that a Money Bill can be introduced:

options.B: In the Rajya Sabha only, with the recommendation of the President
options.C: Only in the Lok Sabha, and that too on the recommendation of the President
options.D: In the Lok Sabha, without the recommendation of the President

q: A tax is sought to be levied by the Government on the strength of an executive instruction alone, without any law made by Parliament. Article 265 of the Constitution bars this because it lays down that:

options.A: All revenues of the Government shall be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: The accounts of the Union shall be kept in the form prescribed by the President
options.C: No money shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund except under an Appropriation Act
options.D: No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law

q: The Contingency Fund of India, from which advances are made to meet unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament, was set up under an Act of Parliament passed in the year:

A body receives a large grant from the Consolidated Fund of India and is, on that account, substantially financed by Government. The audit of its receipts and expenditure by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is provided for in the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under:

options.D: Section 20

q: In the case of a Government company, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India may conduct a supplementary audit of its accounts within the following period from the date of receipt of the audit report of the statutory auditors, under the Companies Act, 2013:

options.D: 120 days

q: A proposal seeks a vote of the Lok Sabha on the salaries, allowances and pensions of the persons serving in the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. Such a vote is not required because the administrative expenses of that office are:

options.A: Voted by the Lok Sabha every year
options.B: Met out of the Public Account of India
options.C: Paid out of the receipts of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department
options.D: Charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India

q: Parliament makes a grant for a special purpose which forms no part of the current service of any financial year, such as a one-time national celebration. Such a grant, made under Article 116 of the Constitution, is an:

options.D: Token grant

q: A controlling officer proposes to meet a shortfall in the Revenue section of a grant by transferring funds from the Capital section of the same grant. Re-appropriation of funds from the Capital section to the Revenue section of the same grant, or vice versa, is:

options.A: Permissible with the sanction of the General Manager
options.C: Permissible with the concurrence of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Permissible only after the accounts of the year are closed

q:
With reference to the structure of the Consolidated Fund of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Consolidated Fund of India is broadly divided into a Revenue Account and a Capital Account.
2. The public debt of the Government of India forms part of the Consolidated Fund of India, and not of the Public Account of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Which of the following receipts of the Government of India is classified as a capital receipt, and not as a revenue receipt?

options.A: Interest receipts on loans given by the Government
options.B: Dividends and profits from public sector undertakings
options.C: Fees, fines and other miscellaneous receipts
options.D: Recoveries of loans and advances given by the Government

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament, which examines the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General relating to public undertakings, was first set up in the year:

The Departmentally Related Standing Committees, which now scrutinise the Demands for Grants of every Ministry after the general discussion on the Budget, were first introduced as a system in the year:
Accountants General in the States and Principal Directors of Audit on the Railways all work within the single organisation headed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, namely:

options.C: The Indian Audit and Accounts Department
options.D: The Indian Revenue Accounts Service

q:
In respect of the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh of Indian Railways, consider the following statements:
1. The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is a non-lapsable fund, so that the unspent balances under it do not lapse at the close of the financial year.
2. The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is utilised for safety-related works, including replacement and renewal of over-aged assets of track, bridges, signalling and rolling stock.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Both 1 and 2

q: Parliament has three recognised Financial Committees. Which of the following committees does NOT belong to that group?

options.A: Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways
options.D: Committee on Public Undertakings

q: When the Public Accounts Committee reports back to Parliament on what the Government has done on the Committee's earlier recommendations, those reports are called:

options.D: Appropriation Reports

q: A competent authority accords a sanction involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India. Under the financial rules, a copy of that sanction is required to be communicated to:

options.C: The Accounts Officer or Audit Officer concerned
options.D: The Finance Commission

q: An audit team, instead of checking every transaction in a unit, first evaluates the unit's internal control system and plans its test checks accordingly. This systems-based approach to audit places its emphasis on:

options.A: Cent-per-cent substantive checking of all transactions
options.B: Checking only the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts
options.C: Auditing only those transactions which are pointed out by the executive
options.D: Evaluating the system of internal control in the audited unit and directing the substantive test checks in the light of that evaluation

q: The members of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament hold office for a term of:

options.D: Five years

q: Unlike his counterpart in the United Kingdom, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India holds a position in relation to Parliament which is correctly described as follows:

options.A: He is an officer of the Lok Sabha, like his counterpart in the United Kingdom
options.B: He is an independent constitutional authority and is not an officer of Parliament
options.C: He functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Finance
options.D: He presents his reports to Parliament through the Minister of Finance

q: During audit, it is noticed that expenditure booked against a grant exceeds the amount voted for that service, although every item was duly sanctioned. The audit scrutiny that detects this failure is:

options.C: Audit against provision of funds, which verifies that the expenditure does not exceed the grant or appropriation and is incurred for the purpose for which the provision was made
options.D: Propriety audit

q: In examining the audited accounts of the Government, one of the foremost duties of the Public Accounts Committee is to satisfy itself, among other things, that:

options.A: The estimates for the coming year have been framed on a realistic basis
options.B: The rate of return on the capital-at-charge of Railways is adequate
options.C: The public undertakings are run on sound commercial principles
options.D: The moneys shown in the accounts as having been disbursed were legally available for, and applicable to, the service or purpose to which they have been applied

q: Moneys received by a Government officer as court deposits in connection with the affairs of the Union, which are neither revenues nor loans credited to the Consolidated Fund, are credited under Article 266(2) of the Constitution to:

options.C: The Consolidated Fund of the State concerned
options.D: A deposit account with the Reserve Bank of India

q: The Railway Safety Fund, utilised primarily for safety works at level crossings, is credited mainly with:

options.A: The dividend received from railway public sector undertakings
options.B: The proceeds of the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares
options.D: Market borrowings raised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation

q: An order re-appropriating funds within a grant is issued in the month of April following the financial year to which the grant relates. For the order to be valid, it must be issued:

options.A: Within three years of the expenditure
options.C: Before the expiry of the financial year to which it relates
options.D: After the accounts of the year are closed

q: Two annual account documents of the Union are often confused with each other. The distinction between the Finance Accounts and the Appropriation Accounts is correctly brought out in which of the following statements?

options.A: The Finance Accounts relate only to Railways, while the Appropriation Accounts relate only to Defence
options.B: The Finance Accounts are prepared by Parliament, while the Appropriation Accounts are prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: There is no difference between the two documents
options.D: The Finance Accounts present the receipts and disbursements of the Government as a whole, while the Appropriation Accounts compare the expenditure with the grants and appropriations for each service

q: Traffic charges are earned by a Railway during March but are actually realised in cash in April. In the commercial accounts of Railways, this situation illustrates the distinction that:

options.A: Earnings represent the amounts earned during the period on the accrual basis, whether or not actually received, while receipts represent the amounts actually realised
options.B: Earnings represent the cash actually received, while receipts represent the amounts due
options.C: There is no distinction between the two terms
options.D: Receipts include the dividend payable to General Finances

q: While vetting the Annual Financial Statement, an accounts officer finds that revenue-account spending and other spending have been merged in a single total. Which constitutional requirement has been breached in the presentation?

options.A: Article 112(2), which requires the estimates to distinguish expenditure on revenue account from other expenditure
options.B: Article 113, which requires every demand to carry the recommendation of the President
options.C: Article 116, which deals with votes on account and votes of credit
options.D: Article 150, which deals with the form in which accounts are kept

q: Midway through the year, a Ministry finds that the amount Parliament authorised for a service will not last the year and seeks more money during the same year itself. Which instrument fits this situation?

options.A: An Excess Grant, voted after the year closes
options.B: A Supplementary Grant, voted during the financial year
options.C: A Vote of Credit for an indefinite demand
options.D: A token grant for a service already fully provided

q: A sudden emergency creates a huge demand on India's resources whose size and indefinite character make it impossible to give the usual budget details. Which grant is designed for exactly this case?

options.C: A Vote of Credit under Article 116
options.D: A Vote on Account under Article 116

q: A private member's Bill is ready for passing, but once enacted it will draw money out of the Consolidated Fund of India, and no Presidential recommendation for its consideration has been obtained. What is the position under Article 117(3)?

options.A: The Bill can be passed if the Speaker permits it
options.B: The Bill can be passed if the Finance Minister concurs
options.C: The Bill can be passed after CAG certification of funds
options.D: The Bill shall not be passed by either House unless the President has recommended its consideration to that House

q: A demand for a grant is placed before the Lok Sabha without the recommendation of the President. Invoking Article 113, the objection that succeeds is:

options.A: No demand for a grant shall be made except on the recommendation of the President
options.B: No demand can be made after the general discussion begins
options.C: Every demand must first be cleared by the Estimates Committee
options.D: Every demand must first be certified by the CAG

q: After the Demands are voted, a member proposes an amendment to the Appropriation Bill shifting a voted amount from one service to another. How does Article 114 treat such an amendment?

options.A: It is allowed in the Lok Sabha but not in the Rajya Sabha
options.B: It shall not be proposed, as it would vary the amount or alter the destination of a grant
options.C: It is allowed with the Finance Minister's consent
options.D: It is allowed for charged expenditure only

q: A dispute arises over who finally prescribes the form in which the accounts of the Union and the States are kept. The correct constitutional position under Article 150 is that the form is prescribed by:

options.B: The CAG on his own authority
options.C: The President, on the advice of the CAG
options.D: The Ministry of Finance

q: The CAG has completed his report relating to the accounts of a State. To whom is that report submitted under Article 151?

options.A: To the President, who lays it before Parliament
options.B: To the Chief Minister of the State
options.C: To the Public Accounts Committee of the State
options.D: To the Governor of the State, who causes it to be laid before the State Legislature

q: A Government officer receives moneys as deposits in connection with Union affairs; the moneys are neither Union revenues nor loans. Following Article 266(2), these moneys are credited to:

options.D: The Railway Reserve Fund

q: Unforeseen expenditure must be met immediately, before Parliament can authorise it. An advance for this purpose may be made from the fund placed at the disposal of:

options.A: The President of India - the Contingency Fund of India
options.B: The Finance Minister - the Public Account of India
options.C: The CAG - the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: The Speaker - the Contingency Fund of India

q: An audit party is tracing every rupee spent out of the Consolidated Fund of India to see that it was applied to the purpose for which the grant was made. This core duty of the CAG over Union and State expenditure is dealt with in the DPC Act, 1971 under:

options.D: Section 13

q: Audit questions the system by which customs receipts are assessed, collected and allocated between heads. The CAG performs this receipts-side scrutiny in exercise of his duty under which section of the DPC Act, 1971?

options.A: Section 17, audit of stores and stock
options.C: Section 16, audit of receipts payable into the Consolidated Fund
options.D: Section 10, compilation of accounts

q: A stores depot's stock accounts are taken up to verify that stores are properly kept and accounted for. Audit of stores and stock kept in Government offices is provided for in the DPC Act, 1971 under:

options.D: Section 20

q: Consider the following statements about audit of a substantially financed body under Section 14 of the DPC Act, 1971: 1. The audit is undertaken where the grant or loan in a financial year is not less than Rs 25 lakh. 2. The audit is undertaken where the grant or loan is not less than 75 per cent of the total expenditure of that body. Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A grant was given to a body for a specific purpose with conditions attached. Instead of re-checking the body's spending himself, the CAG scrutinises how the sanctioning authority satisfied itself that those conditions were fulfilled. This power flows from the DPC Act, 1971 under:

options.D: Section 15

q: The accounts of a Government company are due for audit by the CAG. The provision of the DPC Act, 1971 under which this audit of Government companies is carried out is:

options.D: Section 12

q: An authority is not ordinarily subject to CAG audit, but its audit is specially entrusted to the CAG. Such entrusted audit is provided for in the DPC Act, 1971 under:

options.D: Section 23

q: During an audit, the CAG's party needs to inspect an accounts office and call for its books and papers. The power to inspect any office of accounts and require documents to be sent to him is conferred by the DPC Act, 1971 under:

options.D: Section 15

q: An audit office asks under what authority the principles and procedures in the Regulations on Audit and Accounts bind it. Those Regulations are framed by the CAG under the DPC Act, 1971 in:

options.D: Section 23

q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under Section 10 of the DPC Act, 1971, the CAG is responsible for compiling the accounts of the Union and of each State, unless relieved by the President in the prescribed manner. 2. For Railways, the CAG stands so relieved, and Railway accounts are compiled by the Railway Accounts Department while audit remains with the CAG. Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A State finance department seeks the CAG's help and information in connection with the maintenance of its accounts. The CAG's duty to give information to, and render assistance to, the Union and the States in connection with their accounts is provided in the DPC Act, 1971 under:

options.D: Section 23

q: The report of the CAG on a Government company has to be laid before Parliament. The laying of CAG reports on Government companies and corporations before Parliament or the State Legislature is provided in the DPC Act, 1971 under:

options.D: Section 17

q: An officer appointed as CAG at the age of 61 asks how long he can hold the office. The term of the CAG is:

options.A: Five years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
options.B: Six years or up to the age of 60 years, whichever is earlier
options.C: Five years or up to the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier
options.D: Six years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier

q: A newly elected MP wants to know the composition of the Public Accounts Committee before seeking membership. The Committee consists of:

options.A: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.B: 22 members - 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
options.C: 25 members - 15 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
options.D: 15 members, all from the Rajya Sabha

q: Which committee of Parliament is composed entirely of Lok Sabha members, numbering 30?

options.D: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways

q: A member assumes the Committee on Public Undertakings will examine the CAG's report on Indian Railways. Why is that assumption wrong?

options.A: Railways is a departmental undertaking of the Government, not a public undertaking in the form of a company or corporation
options.B: The Committee has only Lok Sabha members
options.C: Railway accounts are kept secret from Parliament
options.D: Railways is audited by private auditors

q: After the general discussion on the Budget ends, the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways go for examination to a committee of 31 members - 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha. That committee is:

options.D: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways

q: A researcher dates the practice of sending Demands for Grants to Departmentally Related Standing Committees after the general discussion. This committee system was introduced in the year:
During a difficult PAC sitting, members lean heavily on one officer's advice on audit matters. The CAG is traditionally described in relation to the Public Accounts Committee as its:

options.D: Reporting officer

q: A para in the CAG's Report has been examined and the Government must convey its final stand on it. Action Taken Notes conveying that final stand are furnished to:

options.D: The Ministry of Finance

q: An important audit objection survives the executive's replies and is being built up step by step towards the CAG's Report. The correct order in which it matures is:

options.C: Draft Para, then Audit Para, then Provisional Para
options.D: Draft Para, then Provisional Para, then Audit Para

q: A field audit party finishes work in a divisional office and must first tell the executive what it found, before anything escalates. The results of audit in a field unit are communicated in the first instance through:

options.D: The Appropriation Accounts

q: A review asks not whether money was spent regularly, but whether a programme delivered value - examining the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of operations. This is the focus of:

options.D: Local audit

q: Audit criticises a purchase that followed every rule yet was plainly wasteful and imprudent. By going beyond formal regularity to the wisdom, faithfulness and economy of the spending, the audit being exercised is:

options.A: Financial audit, performance audit and compliance audit
options.B: Internal audit, external audit and vigilance audit
options.D: Central audit, local audit and resident audit

q: Which audit engagement ends with the CAG's certificate on the Finance Accounts and the Appropriation Accounts of the Government?

options.D: Certification (financial attest) audit

options.A: Needs the personal approval of the CAG in every case

options.C: Is not permissible from a charged appropriation to a voted grant, or vice versa
options.D: Is permissible only between two charged appropriations

q: Consider the following statements: 1. Funds once surrendered out of a grant cannot be re-appropriated later in the same financial year. 2. Savings surrendered out of a grant remain at the executive's disposal for meeting an excess under another grant. Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A grant still has an unspent balance when the financial year closes, and a department claims it can simply spend the balance next year. The correct position is that the unspent balance:

q: Consider the following statements about cut motions: 1. Cut motions can be moved only in respect of Demands for Grants, that is, voted expenditure. 2. Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India can also be reduced through a cut motion. Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Discussion on the Demands for Grants runs out of allotted time with several Ministries' demands still undebated. The Lok Sabha then puts all outstanding demands to vote together. This procedure is called:

options.D: A token grant

q: A new service is proposed, and the money it needs can in fact be found by re-appropriation within the existing grant, so only a nominal vote is sought to establish the new service. The grant voted in such a case is:

options.D: A Supplementary Grant

q: Consider the following statements: 1. The ordinary working expenses of Indian Railways are accounted for under Major Head 3002 and charged to the Revenue section of the Consolidated Fund of India. 2. The balances of Railway reserve funds such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund are held in the Public Account of India. Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Both 1 and 2

q: An accountant must book transactions relating to the Contingency Fund of India and, separately, the State Provident Funds. In the List of Major and Minor Heads, these are accounted for respectively under Major Heads:

During the Budget debate, a member wishes to move a motion reducing the salary and allowances payable to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, which are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India. What is the correct parliamentary position?

options.A: The item can be voted upon like any other Demand for Grant
options.B: The item can be discussed in either House, but it is not submitted to the vote of Parliament
options.C: The item can neither be discussed nor voted upon in Parliament
options.D: The item can be voted upon only by the Rajya Sabha

q: A zonal Railway met an urgent unforeseen liability in August by taking an advance from the Contingency Fund of India. How is that advance made good to the Fund?

options.A: It is written off against the savings of the Railway at the close of the year
options.B: It is repaid out of the balances held in the Public Account of India
options.C: After Parliament authorises the expenditure, it is recouped by appropriation from the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: It is adjusted automatically when the next Finance Bill is passed

options.A: It requires a fresh Demand for Grant to be voted by the Lok Sabha
options.B: It requires an Appropriation Act before any payment can be made
options.C: It can be paid only after the Comptroller and Auditor General certifies the balance
options.D: It requires no appropriation by Parliament, the Government holding the money as banker or trustee for the depositor

q: While preparing the Annual Financial Statement, the Budget Division must present the estimates of expenditure in a manner that separates one class of spending from the rest. Article 112(2) requires the estimates to distinguish:

options.A: Expenditure on revenue account from other expenditure
options.D: Tax-financed expenditure from borrowing-financed expenditure

q: Two devices are sometimes confused in an election year. The first device is:

options.A: An advance from the Contingency Fund of India
options.B: A Vote on Account voted by the Lok Sabha
options.C: A Vote of Credit for an indefinite demand
options.D: An Excess Grant regularising past spending

q: In November, a Ministry finds that the amount already authorised for a service will fall short before 31 March and seeks more money in the same year; in a second case, accounts of a closed year show spending beyond the grant. Which pairing is correct?

options.A: The first case needs an Excess Grant and the second a Supplementary Grant
options.B: Both cases are met by a Vote on Account
options.C: Both cases are met by a token grant through re-appropriation
options.D: The first case needs a Supplementary Grant during the year and the second an Excess Grant after the close of the year

q: A controlling officer proposes to meet a shortfall under a voted grant by transferring funds available under a charged appropriation of the same Demand. The proposal is:

options.A: Not permissible, as re-appropriation is not allowed from a charged appropriation to a voted grant, or vice versa
options.B: Permissible with the concurrence of the FA&CAO alone

q: Savings are available in the Revenue section of a grant and a works head in the Capital section of the same grant needs additional funds. options.A: Permissible with the sanction of the General Manager
options.B: Permissible with the concurrence of the resident audit office
options.D: Permissible only in the last month of the financial year

q: By October, a division is certain that a large part of its grant for a work will remain unspent because the work has been deferred. Under the financial rules, the anticipated savings should be:

options.C: Utilised on other works of the division without any formal order
options.D: Transferred to a suspense head until the next year

q: A grant voted for 2025-26 remains partly unspent on 31 March 2026 and the department wishes to spend the balance in April 2026 on the same service. The unspent balance:

options.D: Lapses at the close of the year and is available again only if voted afresh by Parliament

options.A: In the like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court

options.C: By a simple-majority resolution of the Lok Sabha alone
options.D: By an order of the Public Accounts Committee confirmed by the Speaker

options.C: Is not eligible for any further office under the Government of India or under the Government of a State
options.D: May accept the office if the Public Accounts Committee recommends it

q: An audit party wishes to trace the statutory basis for the CAG's duty regarding all expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India. In the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, that duty is dealt with in:

options.D: Section 13

q: A receipts-side audit team is checking whether all revenues payable into the Consolidated Fund of India have been duly recovered and credited. The provision of the DPC Act, 1971 under which audit of such receipts is dealt with is:

options.D: Section 23

q: During the audit of a stores depot, the audit party examines the custody, receipt and issue of stock kept in a Government department. This head of audit is provided for in the DPC Act, 1971 under:

options.D: Section 14

q: The accounts of a Government company, in which the Government holds the majority of the paid-up share capital, come up for audit by the CAG. In the DPC Act, 1971, audit of Government companies is provided for under:

options.D: Section 13

q: A specialised authority is not otherwise subject to audit by the CAG, but the President entrusts its audit to him in the public interest. The provision of the DPC Act, 1971 covering audit so entrusted to the CAG is:

options.D: Section 20

q:
Consider the following statements about audit of a body substantially financed by grants or loans from the Consolidated Fund of India, under Section 14 of the DPC Act, 1971:

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: An audited office declines to produce certain files, saying audit has no right to call for them. Under the DPC Act, 1971, the CAG is empowered to:

options.A: Inspect any office of accounts and require any accounts, books, papers and other documents needed for audit to be sent to him
options.B: Stop payment of the bills of that office until the files are produced

options.D: Disallow the entire expenditure of that office for the year

q: A newly posted Accounts officer asks who, under the DPC Act, 1971, carries the responsibility for compiling the accounts of the Union, unless the President relieves the CAG of that responsibility in the prescribed manner. That responsibility is laid down in:

options.D: Section 20

q: A reconstituted Public Accounts Committee has members from both Houses, with the larger contingent coming from the Lok Sabha. The total strength of the Committee and its composition are:
